name: Question 11
worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(2{x}^{2})-\int (2{x}^{2})(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{3}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$ 

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2-2+1)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Evaluate ∫1e4x(log3⁡x)2dx.

a
 e2+2ln2⁡3
b
 8e
c
 e2−1ln2⁡3
d
 2e2−1
e
 1−2eln2⁡3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=(log3⁡x)2⟹dudx=2log3⁡xxln⁡3dvdx=4x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫4xdx=2x2.

This gives ∫4x(log3⁡x)2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡x)2(2x2)−∫(2x2)(2log3⁡xxln⁡3)dx=2x2(log3⁡x)2−4ln⁡3∫xlog3⁡(x)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xlog3⁡(x)dx. We take

u=log3⁡(x)⟹dudx=1xln⁡3dvdx=x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫xdx=x22.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xlog3⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡x)(x22)−∫(x22)(1xln⁡3)dx=x2log3⁡x2−12ln⁡3∫xdx=x2log3⁡x2−x24ln⁡3+D, where D is a constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫4x(log3⁡x)2dx=2x2(log3⁡x)2−4ln⁡3(x2log3⁡x2−x24ln⁡3+D)=2x2(log3⁡x)2−2x2log3⁡xln⁡3+x2ln2⁡3+C=2x2ln2⁡xln2⁡3−2x2ln⁡xln2⁡3+x2ln2⁡3+C=x2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+1)+C, where C=−4Dln⁡3.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log3⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡3.

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: ∫1e4x(log3⁡x)2dx=[x2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+1)]1e=e2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡e−2ln⁡e+1)−12ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡1−2ln⁡1+1)=e2ln2⁡3(2−2+1)−1ln2⁡3(0−0+1)=e2−1ln2⁡3.
